summary.text: 去 commonly means “go away,” “leave,” or “depart.” Its early graph is disputed: it has been read as a person leaving an opening or as a covered vessel, so the original depiction remains uncertain.

formation.text: The early graph’s construction is disputed. One analysis sees a person above an opening and connects the scene with departure; another identifies a covered vessel associated with 盍. Shuowen parses it as 大 plus 凵, treating 凵 as a sound element, but the vessel-cover analysis contests that parsing. A proposed link to 呿, “open the mouth,” is unproven. The suggested path from covering to departure is an interpretation, not a documented sequence.

history.text: The record includes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and Shuowen small-seal forms. The oracle form is described with branching upper strokes above a lower enclosure open at the bottom; the small-seal form also has an open-bottom enclosure. These shapes do not settle what the earliest graph depicts.

Shuowen explains 去 as people parting and parses it as 大 plus 凵, with 凵 supplying sound. Another account reads a person leaving a cave opening. A competing analysis identifies the oracle graph as an early form of 盍 and cites a bronze form of 盍 analyzed as 去 plus 皿. These are competing accounts of the graph’s history.

uncertainties.text: The early graph has been read as a person and opening or as a covered vessel. Departure is not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed, and the proposed connection from covering to departure is not a documented sequence.
A proposal connects 去 with 呿, “open the mouth,” but the evidence does not establish 呿 as the source of 去’s original sound or meaning. Later reading relationships do not prove that origin.

senses.period: Transmitted Zhouyi and Shijing passages, characterized as Western Zhou; exact manuscript dating unresolved
senses.text: The cited departure uses occur in transmitted Zhouyi and Shijing passages characterized as Western Zhou usage; the quoted lines are not independently dated manuscript attestations. Departure is not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed.

senses.gloss: put away; eliminate; get rid of
senses.text: Historical reading records associate 去 with “get rid of” as well as “depart” and distinguish readings for these uses, but do not establish when they arose or how they are related.
In current use, 去 commonly means “go away,” “leave,” or “depart.”

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish whether “get rid of” developed from “depart,” the reverse, or represents a separate historical use. Departure is also not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed.
The proposed ancient readings do not provide an independently established sound comparison proving borrowing from 呿 or identifying the pronunciation of the object depicted in the early graph.
